experiment.purpose: Manual CloudWatch SetAlarmState reason-document admission into a real ECS StepScaling policy at minCapacity=maxCapacity=0; no metric publication or capacity changes.
experiment.queryAgeCases: All age cases use lowercase recentDatapoints without evaluatedDatapoints, startDate approximately600seconds before case construction, and controlled queryDate age. API transit adds approximately0.6–0.9seconds before native Action history.
phases: Initial shape, period mismatch and practical60/120/180second ages

findings.behavior: Lowercase recentDatapoints is sufficient without evaluatedDatapoints in the tested complete reason document; both fields also succeeds. evaluatedDatapoints alone and neither fail. PascalCase RecentDatapoints does not substitute for recentDatapoints.
findings.nativeFailure: Metric data points must be provided
findings.scope: These cases establish the datapoint-field requirement and casing, not requirements for every other reason-document field.

findings.behavior: Fresh period10 reason data supplied to the period60 alarm succeeds, both with and without evaluatedDatapoints. A period mismatch alone therefore does not explain the earlier stale-native-reason failure.

Matching period60 documents with queryDate aged60/120/180seconds fail; period10 documents aged55/180seconds also fail. Fresh controls with startDate600seconds old succeed. With stable recentDatapoints100 and threshold50, these controlled comparisons isolate queryDate freshness rather than alarm/reason period mismatch.
findings.nativeFailure: Scaling deemed unsafe: Error parsing monitor data for <owned alarm>: Monitor data may be null, have an outdated query timestamp, or contain parsing errors

findings.behavior: Focused period60 cases accept requested query ages0 and5seconds, reject15/25/29/30/55/59/60seconds. Observed acceptance at5.743seconds versus rejection at15.603seconds (computed at native Action history timestamps) brackets behavior in this run; no exact cutoff is inferred.
findings.limit: Clock skew, network/processing latency and untested ages prevent a precise universal cutoff, inclusive/exclusive boundary, or period-dependent formula.

findings.behavior: All SetAlarmState calls return HTTP200; Action history distinguishes Succeeded from Failed and retains native error messages. Admission success is not proof of a capacity increase. Native activities report AlreadyAtMaxCapacity/MaxCapacity0, and every observed service has desired/running/pending0.

uncertainties: No exact timestamp-age cutoff is established; notably these observations do not justify either a60second cutoff or an assumed10second cutoff.
queryAgeAtActionHistorySeconds is derived from the submitted queryDate and native history Timestamp, not a server-reported age at its internal validation step.

Only manually triggered StepScaling action admission was tested. No conclusions about metric emission, managed target-tracking alarms, actual capacity transitions, or all possible reason fields follow.
Task-definition deletion returned DELETE_IN_PROGRESS metadata tombstones; ACTIVE definition lists are empty. Final services and clusters are INACTIVE.
